newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels say killed 180 government forces.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels say killed 180 government forces.

text.p: Algeria's Islamic Salvation Army, the armed wing of the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front, said in a statement its guerrillas had killed over 180 security force members in recent clashes in 13 regions across Algeria.

The statement, sent on Thursday to an international news organisation, said that among the government forces killed were about 80 soldiers and paramilitaries shot dead in "fierce confrontations" in the western region of Saida.
It was not possible to verify the statement which was dated February 15.
More than 180 Moslem guerrillas have been killed by the Algerian security forces in Algiers and nearby towns in the past four weeks, according to Algerian newspapers.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against security forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the Islamic Salvation Front had taken a commanding lead.
The front's armed wing is the main rival of the Armed Islamic Group who officials blame for massacres of civilians, mostly in isolated areas around the capital.
